key_concept: The Amazonian rain forest is the richest biodiversity hotspot on Earth, and its approximate species counts per group set the order asked here.
steps: Recall the approximate species counts estimated for the Amazonian rain forest.
Invertebrates (d): more than 1,25,000 species, the largest group.
Mammals (e): about 427 species, the smallest of the five listed.
Descending order is therefore (d) > (a) > (c) > (b) > (e), which matches option (2).
why_not_others: Options (1), (3) and (4) place fishes, mammals or birds at the top. In reality invertebrates (more than 1,25,000) and plants (about 40,000) far outnumber all the vertebrate groups.
common_trap: Students often think birds are the most numerous because they are the most visible, or they swap fishes and birds; fishes (about 3,000) actually outnumber birds (about 1,300).
time_saving_tip: Invertebrates must come first and mammals last. Only option (2) starts with (d) and ends with (e), so you can pick it immediately.
